nodes.label: Authority Rule: architecture wins over module specs

nodes.norm_label: authority rule: architecture wins over module specs

nodes.label: Module 1 — Foundation
nodes.rationale: The only module with no upstream dependencies, consumed by all 39 others; enforces tenancy at the database via RLS rather than application-layer WHERE filters because a forgotten filter leaks PHI and competitors cannot retrofit it.

nodes.label: Seam Registry & Boot-Time Validation (validateSeams)
nodes.rationale: registerSeam/registerEraser plus REQUIRED_SEAMS with deny-stub defaults, validated after module init and before server.listen(); the boot fails when a PHI data class has no DataEraser or a required seam is unregistered — fail-loud at startup rather than at first call.

nodes.label: Outbox Event Catalog (D8)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors M4's audit-action catalog: outbox events cross module boundaries, so the payload schema is a cross-module integration surface deserving boot-validation plus per-call validation. Refuse-on-validation-failure prevents bad events polluting the queue; the publishing transaction rolls back.

nodes.label: Cross-Module Schema Request (CMSR) Registry (D7)
nodes.rationale: Catches the failure mode 'M29 needs an enum value on M4 but the M4 owner doesn't know'. YAML is human-readable, diff-friendly and machine-parseable; a CI rule greps spec PRs for cross-module schema language and asserts a matching approved CMSR exists.

nodes.label: Organization-Settings Registry + validate_organization_settings() Trigger (D6)
nodes.rationale: A trigger on M1's organization table fires regardless of which app-layer service writes the row; putting cross-tenant uniqueness checks in M5's service layer would miss writes coming through the platform-admin route. SECURITY DEFINER + SET search_path + partial UNIQUE index back the uniqueAcrossTenants keys.

nodes.label: RLS Policy Generator (packages/tenancy)
nodes.rationale: A TypeScript generator emitting SQL at migration-authoring time, so consuming modules never call a nonexistent SQL wardenx_enable_rls() function (M04-F07).

nodes.label: withPlatformContext (separately-pooled platform credential, allowlisted)
nodes.rationale: No longer SET ROLE wardenx_admin on the tenant pool: it runs against a separately-pooled platform credential, gated by a platform-job allowlist, with cross-tenant scope audited at severity=critical. wardenx_admin stays confined to migration-runner and break-glass.

nodes.label: App-Layer Envelope Encryption (AES-256-GCM, D1)
nodes.rationale: pgcrypto-symmetric was rejected because key rotation requires a full table rewrite, versus envelope encryption where DEK rotation is a per-row re-wrap. Reused by M2 passkey blobs, M5 identifiers, M22 document storage, M29 HL7 ciphers, M40 BAA metadata.

nodes.label: Outbox Dispatcher Worker (separate container, D4)
nodes.rationale: A separate worker container gives independent scaling, failure isolation from API serving, and independent connection-pool budgeting; in-process is an opt-in for dev/CI only. Max 8 attempts, exponential backoff, outbox.dlq, no silent drop.

nodes.label: Feature Flag Governance (four flag kinds, read-time evaluation D3)
nodes.rationale: Pre-computed-on-org-load was rejected because per-user targeting varies per request (contextHash includes role, location, discipline) and kill-switch activation must propagate globally in under 60 seconds.
nodes.norm_label: feature flag governance (four flag kinds, read-time evaluation d3)

nodes.label: Two-Tier Session Storage (Postgres canonical + Valkey 60s cache, D2)
nodes.rationale: Postgres-only is too slow at the per-request authorize layer (M3's pipeline expects p95 < 3ms); pure-Valkey is too volatile because session data must survive restarts for survey-readiness audit replay.
nodes.norm_label: two-tier session storage (postgres canonical + valkey 60s cache, d2)

nodes.label: Module 2 — Identity & Organization
nodes.rationale: Owns who a user is and which organization a session operates in; owns session machinery/behavior, not the M1-owned tables, reaching them only through M1's exported repositories.

nodes.label: STEP_UP_POLICY (platform floor, tenant-tighten-only, D9)
nodes.rationale: Platform floor {webauthn, totp} with 300s freshness; SMS is deliberately absent (no public-key proof of possession, SIM-swap exposure). The intersect-on-tighten semantic is what makes tenant override safe — a tenant can shrink the trust surface but never expand it.

nodes.label: SESSION_POLICY (one constant for all timeouts, D1)
nodes.rationale: Architecture §7's stricter 15-minute idle governs over Security Hardening's 30-minute for shared clinical workstations; screen-lock and idle are distinct layers.
nodes.norm_label: session_policy (one constant for all timeouts, d1)

nodes.label: Four Session Classes (staff, auditor, external_collaborator, funeral_home)
nodes.norm_label: four session classes (staff, auditor, external_collaborator, funeral_home)

nodes.label: Login-MFA-Counts-As-Step-Up Rule (D10)
nodes.rationale: A clinician who just authenticated with WebAuthn to start a shift should be able to immediately rotate a credential or accept an SUD-unredact request without a second challenge; the 5-minute window keeps a long-lived session from drifting past freshness. External-collaborator and funeral-home sessions get NULL, a hard boundary against privileged action.

nodes.label: AuditorSessionMinter seam (M2 mints, M3 scopes — D4)
nodes.rationale: M2 owns session mechanics; M3 owns engagement scope and window. Boot validation means an engagement that cannot mint a session fails at startup rather than at first use.
nodes.norm_label: auditorsessionminter seam (m2 mints, m3 scopes — d4)

nodes.label: One-Identity-Many-Memberships Model
nodes.rationale: Traveling/contract clinicians legitimately work at more than one agency; authentication factors are user-level and shared, authorization is not. Competitors use single-org logins with bolt-on MFA and force manual account juggling.

nodes.label: HIBP k-anonymity Breached-Password Check (D5)
nodes.rationale: Only a SHA-1 prefix leaves the perimeter, so no PHI and no BAA required; wrapped in an adapter with a circuit breaker that accepts the password and flags for async re-check when HIBP is down.

nodes.label: Module 3 — Authorization
nodes.rationale: The second and third defense-in-depth layers on top of M1's RLS; differentiator is enforced minimum-necessary via ABAC where legacy hospice EHRs ship coarse RBAC and every nurse sees the whole census.

nodes.label: Authorization Resolution Pipeline (RLS → RBAC → ABAC)
nodes.rationale: Deny by default — a missing ABAC binding on a PHI action is a bug, not an allow. Existence non-leak returns 404 where a 403 would reveal a resource the user should not know exists. Authorization scope is pushed into the WHERE clause, never fetch-then-filter.

nodes.label: ABAC Named-Predicate Registry (not a generic rules engine)
nodes.rationale: Predicates are typed functions bound to actions in code and evaluated against server-controlled context; a generic rules engine is an explicit architecture §25 anti-pattern. Cross-module predicates are boot-registered provider seams with deny-stub defaults so M3 never reads a non-dependency table.
nodes.norm_label: abac named-predicate registry (not a generic rules engine)

nodes.label: Break-Glass Emergency Access (D1)
nodes.rationale: 4-hour time-box; co-sign not required for emergency but required for non-emergency, because emergency access must be instant while non-emergency gets the accountability of a second signer. Every access under glass is audited at critical severity.

nodes.label: REQUIRED_SEAMS Registry (D8)
nodes.rationale: Centralizes the seam-binding contract so missing providers fail fast at boot rather than at first call, and gives survey readiness a queryable map of who-consumes-whose-seam. M1 owns the registry and gate; M3 owns the schema of a seam declaration and contributes entries at init, since M1 cannot import an M3-owned registry.

nodes.label: Module mN. Namespace Ownership (D9)
nodes.rationale: Every module owns exactly its mN. prefix for outbox events, audit actions and alert payload types; cross-namespace emission is forbidden. Gives unambiguous provenance, grep-friendly debugging, and prevents namespace squatting. M1's event catalog and M4's action catalog enforce ownership at registration.

nodes.label: Permission Catalog (code-owned, per-module fragments, arch:permissions CI)
nodes.norm_label: permission catalog (code-owned, per-module fragments, arch:permissions ci)

nodes.label: Role Catalog with system_locked CoP Permission Floor
nodes.rationale: Platform templates are cloned per org at onboarding so tenants own their catalog and may rename/disable/extend; the CoP-required floor is protected by system_locked roles that the role editor refuses to edit below.
nodes.norm_label: role catalog with system_locked cop permission floor

nodes.label: Effective-Permission Cache (event-driven invalidation + 60s TTL, D6)
nodes.rationale: Correctness first — no stale elevated access — with a bounded TTL backstop; invalidated on role grant/revoke and role-permission edits, with permissions.changed pushed to affected users (the one permitted direct Socket.IO emit).

nodes.label: Module 4 — Audit & Compliance Log
nodes.rationale: M1 created the place audit lives; M4 makes the log complete, queryable, provably intact and lifecycle-managed. Differentiators are trigger-enforced write capture, first-class Accounting of Disclosures and provable integrity versus competitors' silent cron deletes.

nodes.label: PHI Write-Audit Trigger Generator
nodes.rationale: A generated PostgreSQL trigger on every PHI table records INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with a PHI-scrubbed before/after diff — the guarantee that no clinical mutation escapes the log even via a code path that forgot to call the helper. Runs SECURITY DEFINER owned by wardenx_audit_writer with hardened search_path.

nodes.label: PHI Read-Audit Capture (auditRead + route declaration)
nodes.rationale: DB-level read auditing is too expensive, so reads are captured at the resource handler. Granularity is aggregate for list views and individual for chart opens and all disclosures — individual events are the §164.528-relevant ones; row-granular list views would explode volume with no compliance gain.

nodes.label: Accounting of Disclosures (HIPAA §164.528 / 42 CFR §2.13 scopes, D11)
nodes.rationale: A single endpoint conflated two regulatory regimes with different scopes, lookbacks (6-year vs lifetime) and patient rights; the scope parameter keeps backward compatibility while enabling the Part 2 right. The accounting request itself is audited at the matching retention class.
nodes.norm_label: accounting of disclosures (hipaa §164.528 / 42 cfr §2.13 scopes, d11)

nodes.label: compliance_42cfr_part2 Retention Class (D8)
nodes.rationale: Part 2 pins no numeric retention, but §2.13's accounting right effectively requires lifetime retention; industry practice is lifetime + 6 years post-death. The eraser refuses even under an approved destruction certificate so tenant offboarding cannot silently erase Part 2 audit data while patients are alive.

nodes.label: PHI Denylist Categories (pii_high_sensitivity / sud_value / narrative_free_text, D10)
nodes.rationale: The flat column-name denylist did not scale: every module had to remember SSN, and the SUD case introduced a row-conditional denylist the flat list could not express. Categories give declarative intent that the generator translates to columns; sud_value is forced on any compliance_42cfr_part2 action as defense in depth.
nodes.norm_label: phi denylist categories (pii_high_sensitivity / sud_value / narrative_free_text, d10)

nodes.label: Certificate-of-Destruction Workflow + DataEraser Registry (D4)
nodes.rationale: Keeps one auditable workflow and one certificate format while each module retains responsibility for its own storage erasure; a forgotten eraser is a failed boot, never silent data loss. A refusing eraser returns partial_refused; legal-hold/Part 2 propagation uses the HoldApplier seam.

nodes.label: Audit Action Catalog & mN.<resource>.<verb> Convention (D9)
nodes.rationale: With 40+ modules the catalog needs structure; the prefix makes provenance unambiguous and lets M4 enforce module-ownership at boot. The optional _from_<source> suffix lets survey readiness distinguish operator-driven from external-event-driven actions.

nodes.label: Disclosure Classification Inferred from Integration Egress (D5)
nodes.rationale: Any read served through the FHIR Gateway, portal, external-collaborator or funeral-home session is recorded as *.disclosed with {to, purpose}; internal staff reads are *.viewed. This captures the real §164.528 surface — data leaving the perimeter — automatically, with a manual marking path for off-system sends like faxes.
nodes.norm_label: disclosure classification inferred from integration egress (d5)

nodes.label: Cyclic Reach-Through Inverted to Boot-Registered Seams (M04-F01)
nodes.rationale: The destruction eraser, Part 2 accounting, terminology resolution and certificate rendering would each create a dependency cycle if they imported M5/M29/M38/M22; they are inverted to PatientLifecycleProvider, SudClassResolver and CertificatePdfRenderer seams whose types live in packages/types and which validateSeams() enforces.
nodes.norm_label: cyclic reach-through inverted to boot-registered seams (m04-f01)

nodes.label: Module 5 — Patient & Demographics (the patient spine)
nodes.rationale: The canonical identity of every person receiving hospice care and the spine every other clinical module hangs off; the bet is that precise, auditable identity hygiene is a real competitive advantage in survey readiness.

nodes.label: Patient Matching Pipeline (deterministic-first, probabilistic queued, D2)
nodes.rationale: Matches the IIS/EMPI consensus of deterministic + probabilistic + human review. Auto-merge is FORBIDDEN at any score because it creates the irreversible-merge class of disaster; tenant tuning is bounded (≥0.85 hard floor, ≤0.80 soft ceiling) so messy-intake agencies can adjust without code change.
nodes.norm_label: patient matching pipeline (deterministic-first, probabilistic queued, d2)

nodes.label: PatientReader Seam (exactly six methods, D11)
nodes.rationale: Pinned to the six methods T-29.05's cascade needs — extra methods would tempt M29 into M5-shaped queries the dependency-cruiser forbids. Every result routes through patientResolver so merge-redirect is transparent, preventing bugs where a cascade returns the post-merge patient at L1 but the pre-merge patient at L4. 200ms p95 is a hard SLO.

nodes.label: PatientMutator Seam (field allowlist, SSN silently dropped, D12)
nodes.rationale: The mutator is the choke point enforcing 'ignore SSN even if the lab sends it' — defense in depth against PID-19 carrying sensitive identifiers from a chatty partner. MRN immutability prevents an external system rewriting M5's canonical identifier; status and merge transitions stay internal-only.
nodes.norm_label: patientmutator seam (field allowlist, ssn silently dropped, d12)

nodes.label: CaseloadProvider Seam (patient_assignment ∪ M17 active-shift visits, D4)
nodes.rationale: M3's caseload_membership ABAC needs a real provider and M5 is the only module with the primary-care-team truth; M17 contributes the on-shift reality. Boot validation refuses to start without registration — fail-loud at boot, never silent at runtime.
nodes.norm_label: caseloadprovider seam (patient_assignment ∪ m17 active-shift visits, d4)

nodes.label: Append-Only Address History (D5)
nodes.rationale: Addresses carry compliance weight — state-Medicaid eligibility, Part 2 state overlay, RHC-vs-SNF place of service, routing geofence, §164.514 de-identification — so in-place UPDATE would lose prior state required for backdated audits.

nodes.label: PrivacyFlag Snapshot (M39 source of truth, deny-on-stale, D3)
nodes.rationale: A million reads a day cannot hit M39 each time (performance), a stale snapshot must never grant (safety), and every flip is an event recomputable from M39 history (auditability). A quarterly full rebuild reconciles drift.
nodes.norm_label: privacyflag snapshot (m39 source of truth, deny-on-stale, d3)

nodes.label: §164.526 Right to Amend Workflow (60-day SLA, D9)
nodes.rationale: The HIPAA right is operational, not aspirational; the SLA alarm is the only thing that keeps it from quietly slipping, and the statement of disagreement is the deny path's required regulatory artifact that travels with every subsequent disclosure.
nodes.norm_label: §164.526 right to amend workflow (60-day sla, d9)

nodes.label: Merge via patient_resolver Redirect (reversible 30 days, D8)
nodes.rationale: Resolver-based redirect preserves audit referential integrity instead of destructively UPDATE-ing satellite tables; the 30-day reversibility window matches the typical 'we just realized' lag, and restricting late unmerge to platform break-glass keeps it from becoming routine.
nodes.norm_label: merge via patient_resolver redirect (reversible 30 days, d8)

nodes.label: Selective Envelope Encryption (SSN + state ID only, D6)
nodes.rationale: Minimum-necessary encryption surface: encryption applies where the column would otherwise be a privacy-impact magnet. MBI is the non-sensitive Medicare surrogate and stays plaintext; over-encryption breaks search and joins without compensating risk reduction.
nodes.norm_label: selective envelope encryption (ssn + state id only, d6)

nodes.label: Module 6 — Admission, Election & Certification
nodes.rationale: Owns the regulatory state of the hospice relationship — the module a CMS surveyor opens first. The differentiator is making the regulatory state impossible to enter into a non-compliant configuration, so M23's claim layer has nothing to reject.

nodes.label: Election Period & Benefit-Period Sequencing (D9 transfer-in inheritance)
nodes.rationale: The receiving hospice inherits the period sequence per 42 CFR 418.28; restarting the counter would over-state benefit days and trigger MAC rejection at NOE submission. F2F requirements follow the inherited sequence — a 3rd-or-later period requires F2F regardless of which hospice held it.
nodes.norm_label: election period & benefit-period sequencing (d9 transfer-in inheritance)

nodes.label: Certification of Terminal Illness (CTI) with late oral-then-written path (D3, D4)
nodes.rationale: Attending signature is required on period-1 only (418.22(c) requires only the medical director on recerts). Late certs record the oral verbal cert and compute a written-cert deadline of period start + 2 calendar days; the admission is flagged but NOT auto-held because some MD signatures arrive at the 50th hour and auto-hold would create false positives.
nodes.norm_label: certification of terminal illness (cti) with late oral-then-written path (d3, d4)

nodes.label: Face-to-Face Encounter Compliance Artifact (D2, D5)
nodes.rationale: F2F is a compliance fact tied to 418.22(a)(4)/418.25, not just another encounter type; co-storing in M8 would force duplicating window_start/window_end/attestation/override fields onto every encounter row and lose the strict 30-day window semantics. The override lives on the F2F row itself to avoid a dual-truth 'which is the source of compliance' problem.

nodes.label: Compliance Window Engine (regulatory clocks as outbox events)
nodes.rationale: Assessment clocks live in M6 as compliance_window rows because M9 has no compliance-window primitive and M30 would otherwise query two modules to render the queue. Window math is computed in the org timezone because CMS regulation is calendar-day oriented and surveyors think in local time; UTC-only would mis-classify late certs.
nodes.norm_label: compliance window engine (regulatory clocks as outbox events)

nodes.label: AdmissionEventApplier (external HL7 narrow rails, D13/D14)
nodes.rationale: M6's state machines are clinical compliance artifacts; letting external input drive them would create non-repudiable survey risk (an admit not signed by the hospice MD, an F2F not attested by an NP). Permitted mutations are exactly death-discharge under strict preconditions, informational compliance windows, and referral withdrawal. Contract violations are logged and refused rather than thrown, so one partner's malformed payload cannot dead-letter the shared consumer queue for all tenants.

nodes.label: Level-of-Care Period + GIP Documentation Gate (D12)
nodes.rationale: GIP is the highest-paying and most-audited level of care; forcing the three attestations at the moment of state change creates a strong audit trail and prevents retroactive justification. Capturing documentation later in a separate flow invites surveyor findings and loses the temporal binding.

nodes.label: NOE/NOTR Wire-Artifact Ownership Belongs to M23 (D1)
nodes.rationale: NOE is a claim-adjacent artifact governed by 837I/UB-04 mechanics — billing competencies, not clinical. The clinical EHR signs the election and emits the event; the billing system tells CMS. Putting NOE in M6 would bloat it with claim-cycle state and couple it to MAC connection lifecycle.
nodes.norm_label: noe/notr wire-artifact ownership belongs to m23 (d1)

nodes.label: For-Cause Discharge Medical-Director Cosign (D11)
nodes.rationale: For-cause discharge is the highest-risk patient-rights event in hospice operations; the medical-director cosign is both a clinical-leadership check and a survey defense. A single-step action would risk inappropriate use, and surveyors expect dual-signature evidence.

nodes.label: Module 7 — Care Plan (IPOC)
nodes.rationale: Owns the Individualized Plan of Care surveyors inspect most directly; competitors ship a flat problem list with a free-text plan field and an IDG-review checkbox that enforces no content, producing the two classic citations of review-without-revision and clinical-only goals.

nodes.label: Hybrid Versioning: mutable rows + immutable state_snapshot (D1)
nodes.rationale: A surveyor asking 'what was the plan on day N' gets a deterministic answer from the snapshot while the clinician hot path stays on mutable rows. Per-version row duplication would balloon storage and complicate edit ergonomics; mutable-rows-plus-audit-only loses point-in-time fidelity to a survey-grade standard.
nodes.norm_label: hybrid versioning: mutable rows + immutable state_snapshot (d1)

nodes.label: CARE_PLAN_GATES — 5-day initial and 15-day review encounter-sign gates (D2, D3)
nodes.rationale: The gate is on encounter signing, not chart access — a clinician can always read and document; the system blocks committing the visit. A hard gate at day 15 would trigger constant overrides on weekend-overlapping cycles, so a 3-day grace plus an audited override keeps a real agency moving without surrendering enforcement.
nodes.norm_label: care_plan_gates — 5-day initial and 15-day review encounter-sign gates (d2, d3)

nodes.label: RequiredSignerSet Quorum Constants (D5)
nodes.rationale: Capturing the required signer set at version-open time rather than evaluating at sign time makes survey reconstruction deterministic. The IDG physician seat is MD/DO only per ADR-0018 D3 — an NP may sign the INITIAL plan as attending but may not occupy the CoP 418.56 IDG physician role.

nodes.label: IdgDecisionPayload Outbox Seam (D4)
nodes.rationale: Even though the dependency direction permits M14 to call applyIdgDecision directly, the outbox is the canonical wire so a meeting decision never silently disappears under retries; the recovery story is M1's dispatcher, not a bespoke retry in M14, and a single typed payload prevents shape drift.

nodes.label: Patient-Stated Goal Verbatim Preservation (D6)
nodes.rationale: original_text is NOT NULL and immutable after creation via CHECK constraint, service guard and audit trigger — direct schema-level enforcement of the CoP 418.56(c) patient-and-family-goals rule, discoverable in survey without relying on a clinician convention.

nodes.label: Single Consent Seam to M39 with sud_disclosure_allowed / dpoa_active predicates (D7)
nodes.rationale: One seam, one consent query, two predicates: M39 owns consent state, M3 owns ABAC mechanics, M7 owns the predicates' meaning for care-plan content. SUD redaction is applied as a SQL WHERE filter, never post-fetch, so there is no 'data loaded but UI-hidden' risk.
nodes.norm_label: single consent seam to m39 with sud_disclosure_allowed / dpoa_active predicates (d7)

nodes.label: Module 8 — Encounters & Visit Notes
nodes.rationale: The clinical record's documentation surface and the nervous-system trigger for clinical-record-driven downstream work; encounter.signed drives half the clinical phase (M9, M10, M14, M22, M28, M31, M33).

nodes.label: HearthNote Three-Layer Documentation Engine
nodes.rationale: Layer 1 deterministic is the structured source of truth, Layer 2 is an enhancement that diffs against Layer 1 and hard-blocks new facts, Layer 3 is the always-on signing-blocking compliance gate. Competitors' AI assistants produce plausible narrative with no seam to the underlying data, so surveyors cannot reconstruct what the clinician picked versus what the AI invented.

nodes.label: Layer-2 Eligibility Three-Flag AND + BAA Gate (D5, D6/M08-F01)
nodes.rationale: Tenant flag alone is too coarse for high-stakes notes and per-clinician only is too granular to audit; the three-flag AND lets a tenant adopt Layer 2 broadly while keeping F2F, admission and recert deterministic-only. No PHI may leave the perimeter until external.anthropic_baa_executed is set — the BAA is recorded as in negotiation, so layer2_eligibility_reason='baa_not_executed' and M32's cloud backend hard-refuses dispatch.
nodes.norm_label: layer-2 eligibility three-flag and + baa gate (d5, d6/m08-f01)

nodes.label: LLM Diff Hard-Block Category List (D7)
nodes.rationale: The three architecture categories (vitals, doses, codes) are insufficient — allergies and code status carry higher safety risk than vitals: a medication-dose error is at least detectable on read, whereas a silently swapped code-status statement may not be. Categories live in one typed constant so adding one is a deliberate reviewed change.

nodes.label: Addenda as First-Class Rows, Immutability After Sign (D2)
nodes.rationale: Surveyor reconstruction of 'what was signed at 4pm on the 12th' needs the row, not the row's edit history; allowing post-sign edits with an audit diff fails the strictest survey defense. An immutability trigger refuses UPDATEs to protected columns and all DELETEs.
nodes.norm_label: addenda as first-class rows, immutability after sign (d2)

nodes.label: Cosignature Workflow — 24h soft / 48h hard, billing-blocked (D3)
nodes.rationale: A 7-day window is too loose for survey defense and no hard cap creates aged billing that ages out; the supervisor-release path past 48 hours (with a ≥40-char documented reason) is the operational concession that makes the gate workable in real agencies.

nodes.label: Three-Tier Late-Entry Ladder (D4)
nodes.rationale: No limit invites fraudulent backdating; a hard 24-hour cap is clinically unrealistic for field staff with offline patches. Three tiers match the operational reality that most late entries are within 24 hours, a few are 1–14 days, and rare admin escalations exceed 14 days.

nodes.label: EVV-Authoritative Encounter Bracketing with Documented Fallback (D9)
nodes.rationale: When M18 events exist they are read-only truth and clinician-entered times cannot override; when absent, a ≥20-char evv_missing_reason is required. Clinician-entered-always defeats EVV; EVV-required breaks offline field work. Stricter than several competitors and earns straight survey defense in Cures Act §12006 states.
nodes.norm_label: evv-authoritative encounter bracketing with documented fallback (d9)

nodes.label: Vocabulary Version Pinned at First Finalize (D11)
nodes.rationale: Latest-version resolution would silently change historical notes when annual ICD-10 and biannual SNOMED updates ship, failing surveyor reconstruction. Pinning freezes the narrative like an immutable git ref — the analog of M7's hybrid versioning.
nodes.norm_label: vocabulary version pinned at first finalize (d11)

nodes.label: BillableEncounterReader Seam
nodes.rationale: M8 exposes a clean reader saying billable / not yet billable / not billable with a reason, factoring cosignature, late-entry, EVV and encounter type — without knowing HIPPS, revenue codes, 837I segments, SIA add-ons or cap math, all of which are M23/M24/M26.

nodes.label: SignedEncountersReader Seam (signedEncountersForPatientSince)
nodes.rationale: M8 is the source of truth, not the digest — the IDG aggregation content is owned by M14 and reads through this seam rather than M8 pre-aggregating.

nodes.label: F2F Dual-Write in One Transaction (D1)
nodes.rationale: Writing both the M8 clinical note and the M6 face_to_face_encounter in one transaction avoids losing HearthNote and EVV for the F2F note while avoiding bloating M8 with compliance fields; if either side's gate fails the transaction aborts and both panels surface remediation.

nodes.label: 5-Minute Step-Up Auth on Every Clinical Signature (D13)
nodes.rationale: No step-up fails 21 CFR Part 11 e-signature principles and CoP 418.104(c) authentication; 5 minutes matches M2's SESSION_POLICY screen-lock window so the whole session-class model stays symmetric.
nodes.norm_label: 5-minute step-up auth on every clinical signature (d13)

nodes.label: Module 9 — Clinical Assessments Suite
nodes.rationale: Where M8 owns the narrative of what happened, M9 owns the numbers that quantify decline and their longitudinal series — the most-asked-for artifact in a hospice CMS survey. The bet is that the alert, trend, reconstruction and consent gating are the differentiated half, not per-form ergonomics.

nodes.label: Shared clinical_assessment Base Table + per-scale data jsonb (D1)
nodes.rationale: One hot table preserves an efficient latest(patientId, scaleType) index, keeps partitioning trivial at one monthly cadence, and lets M14/M22/M28 read a uniform shape; per-scale TypeBox restores the strict validation a generic table would lose. One-table-per-scale means 14 partition sets and a fragile union view.
nodes.norm_label: shared clinical_assessment base table + per-scale data jsonb (d1)

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative Score Computation (D6)
nodes.rationale: Scores feed alerts, IDG packets and M10's HOPE items; a client-trusted score would let a misbehaving or compromised client suppress significant-change alerts by under-scoring. Computing once server-side means chart, trend, FHIR export and CTI narrative all show the same canonical number.

nodes.label: Significant-Change Detection with Platform Floors, Tenant-Tighten-Only (D2)
nodes.rationale: The PAINAD/ESAS-r/Braden/Morse evidence base sets a clinical floor below which silence is unsafe; a loosened threshold would let a tenant suppress alerts the platform considers mandatory. Tightening is the tenant choosing to be more cautious. Detection runs inside the recordAssessment transaction.
nodes.norm_label: significant-change detection with platform floors, tenant-tighten-only (d2)

nodes.label: ScaleSeriesProvider / LatestAssessmentProvider Seams (D7)
nodes.rationale: Two interfaces are M9's entire public surface, so M9 can swap to a materialized backing later without a single consumer changing; direct table reads would couple every consumer to M9's partition and RLS internals.

nodes.label: Scale License Registry with Form-Gating (D3)
nodes.rationale: PPS, FAST, GDS, Braden and Morse IP holders require per-organization licensure evidence; the cleanest legal posture is refusing to capture new measurements when the license lapses while preserving clinical history recorded under a prior active license. Most vendors ship these as fields and trust the tenant — a recurring small survey finding.

nodes.label: Discipline × Scale Eligibility Typed Matrix (D8)
nodes.rationale: CoP ties certain assessments to specific disciplines; encoding it as a typed matrix surfaces violations in CI rather than at runtime. Per-tenant configurability was rejected because it invites tenants to weaken a CoP-driven boundary.

nodes.label: Append-Only Correction-of-Record Amendment (D9)
nodes.rationale: A correction inserts a new row referencing corrects_assessment_id and a trigger marks the prior row superseded; update-in-place destroys the original value's row identity and soft-delete-plus-reinsert loses the explicit 'this corrects that' linkage.

nodes.label: 42 CFR Part 2 Gates Disclosure, Not Record Creation (D10 / M09-F05)
nodes.rationale: The v0.2 design blocking AIMS writes without a release was reversed: Part 2 governs disclosure distinctly from HIPAA and does not bar the treating program from recording SUD data. Gating creation would suppress clinically necessary tardive-dyskinesia surveillance; the obligation attaches when the record leaves the treating program, so the gate moves to every read/FHIR/portal/AoD egress boundary and M39-down now fails disclosure closed rather than blocking writes.
nodes.norm_label: 42 cfr part 2 gates disclosure, not record creation (d10 / m09-f05)

nodes.label: Module 10 — HOPE Engine
nodes.rationale: Exists so a 4-percentage-point APU shortfall (roughly $80–120k of annual margin at median census) is structurally impossible; competitors implemented HOPE as a form because CMS mandated it, but not the regulatory engine around the form.

nodes.label: Five RFA Timepoints (Admission, HUV1, HUV2, SFV, Discharge)
nodes.rationale: Auto-scheduled from M6's admission.activated so a missed window is a workflow failure, not a data-entry one; most legacy vendors implement HOPE as 'open the form when the nurse remembers'.
nodes.norm_label: five rfa timepoints (admission, huv1, huv2, sfv, discharge)

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative J2051 SFV Trigger (2 calendar days from visit date, D3/D4)
nodes.rationale: The clock anchors to the HOPE assessment's visit date, never to signed_at — anchoring to signature would let a clinician extend a federal deadline simply by delaying signing, silently under-reporting HQRP non-compliance. Evaluation is server-side so a client cannot suppress the SFV by under-reporting severity, and exactly one SFV is created per triggering timepoint regardless of how many symptoms cross the threshold.
nodes.norm_label: server-authoritative j2051 sfv trigger (2 calendar days from visit date, d3/d4)

nodes.label: Soft-Window + Hard-Cutoff Timepoint Enforcement (D2, D12)
nodes.rationale: Hard-blocking at window close drives chart back-dating, the worst possible response; a typed late_reason_code from a closed CMS-aligned codelist captures the deviation honestly and feeds the HQRP counter, with a rare auditable admin override past the late deadline.

nodes.label: iqies-client
nodes.rationale: The CMS HOPE submission spec evolves on a different cadence than the manual, so isolating transport, XML envelope and credentials in an adapter lets schema-version bumps land without touching the module. Batch-per-ProviderEntity matches CMS's batching expectation and the one-credential-per-PE-per-MAC submitter model; per-assessment HTTP would race rate limits and break per-batch acceptance semantics.

nodes.label: HopeTimepointProvider / HopeSubmissionProvider / HopeJ2051Provider Seams (D10)
nodes.rationale: Three semantic surfaces rather than one omnibus seam — a consumer wanting the J2051 trajectory should not also get the iQIES submission surface. Direct table reads would make an annual CMS manual revision a six-module change.

nodes.label: Append-Only Correction RFA with iQIES Linkage (D7)
nodes.rationale: CMS requires the original to remain on file at iQIES with the correction explicitly linked; update-in-place would destroy the audit trail and iQIES has no concept of an updated record. The Correction RFA is queued rather than sent immediately so it does not break the batch model or race the original's in-flight acceptance.
nodes.norm_label: append-only correction rfa with iqies linkage (d7)

nodes.label: PPS / ESAS-r Snapshot Frozen at HOPE Sign (D8)
nodes.rationale: A live read of M9 values on every HOPE row read would let a later M9 correction silently mutate the submitted HOPE row — an audit catastrophe. The snapshot preserves what the clinician saw at sign time, which is what was submitted to iQIES.
nodes.norm_label: pps / esas-r snapshot frozen at hope sign (d8)

nodes.label: Tier-Decoupled Capture (Tier 2) vs iQIES Submission (Tier 3)
nodes.rationale: Missing a timepoint cannot be recovered after the window closes, so visit-time entry must keep working during a degradation event; batch submission can wait 24 hours because the deadline is 30 days from completion. hope_assessment writes never depend on iQIES adapter health.

nodes.label: Single data jsonb for CMS HOPE Sections (D1, D11)
nodes.rationale: CMS revises the HOPE manual annually; a column-per-section schema would make each revision a six-week schema change, and a row-per-section schema would force a nine-row join on every M30 measure query. Single jsonb with TypeBox absorbs revisions as a code change, not a schema change.
nodes.norm_label: single data jsonb for cms hope sections (d1, d11)

nodes.label: Module 11 — Orders (clinical-order spine)
nodes.rationale: Every non-medication clinical intervention flows through a single authenticated auditable order; M11 also owns the signature primitive that M12 and any future order-producing module consume.

nodes.label: order_record Spine + per-kind TypeBox data jsonb (D1)
nodes.rationale: Adding a kind is a per-kind TypeBox sub-PR, never an ALTER TABLE; CMS revises CoP 418.104/106 interpretations periodically and the per-kind TypeBox absorbs the churn.
nodes.norm_label: order_record spine + per-kind typebox data jsonb (d1)

nodes.label: Seven-State XState Order Lifecycle Machine (D2)
nodes.rationale: XState gives compile-time exhaustiveness — every transition named, every guard typed, every side effect in one place. Ad-hoc booleans like is_signed/is_discontinued drift and produce illegal combinations; a five-state model without verbal_pending and expired_unsigned loses the CMS 418.104(b) compliance signal.

nodes.label: 48-Hour Verbal-Order Window, Platform Floor Tenant-Tighten-Only (D3)
nodes.rationale: CMS sets 'reasonable time'; industry and most state-board codifications land at 48 hours with stricter state rules common. The platform floor protects tenants from configuring an unsafe-from-survey window while allowing tightening to as short as 1 hour; auto-detecting state from patient address was rejected as too fragile for travelling clinicians.

nodes.label: Polymorphic OrderSignatureProvider Seam (target_kind discriminator, D4)
nodes.rationale: A polymorphic FK in PostgreSQL is messy, so integrity is enforced at the application layer through the typed seam. M11 owns the signature primitive, verbal timer and cosign workflow once; M12 consumes without M11 importing M12 — avoiding a dependency-graph cycle.

nodes.label: Standing-Order Template + Spawned-Instance Engine (D5)
nodes.rationale: Standing orders in hospice are signature-anchored — the medical director signs the template and spawns inherit the signature per CMS interpretation; re-signing each spawn would generate clinician fatigue and contradict the regulatory reading. Per ADR-0019 D2 the spawner runs only against an authorized prescriber's signed protocol, carrying the authorizing-protocol reference and prescriber identity.

nodes.label: Discontinuation as Command + Cascade with Its Own Row (D13)
nodes.rationale: The discontinuation row is the audit anchor preserving actor, reason, effective time and cascade attribution — a bare status flip loses all of it and turns 'show me everything discontinued for adverse event last quarter' into an unqueryable audit-event scan. Mirrors M6's revocation/discharge command+cascade.
nodes.norm_label: discontinuation as command + cascade with its own row (d13)

nodes.label: Orthogonal Lab Transmission & Results Lifecycle (D16, D17, D18, D19)
nodes.rationale: Transmission retry is M29-owned and M11 only observes, because duplicating the backoff loop would double-execute. Result attachment does NOT auto-complete the order — 42 CFR 418.106 requires documented clinician review of significant findings, so the active→completed transition stays a clinician decision. The lab-observation back-reference is a single latest-pointer UUID with no cross-module FK; full history stays in M29's authoritative link table.
nodes.norm_label: orthogonal lab transmission & results lifecycle (d16, d17, d18, d19)

nodes.label: OrderProvider Seam (getOrdersSince / findActiveOrder / timeliness)
nodes.rationale: Lets M11 ship today and M12/M14/M21/M23/M28/M30/M33 attach when they lock; the dependency-cruiser boundary check enforces that consumers may not import M11's Drizzle schema, only the seam types.

nodes.label: Assessment-Trigger Banner as Derived Valkey Projection (D7)
nodes.rationale: Storing a suggestion as a first-class entity invites auto-approve and bulk-approve workflows that bypass clinical judgement; the derived TTL-bounded projection keeps M9/M10 as the source of truth while the order's triggering_*_id preserves the audit trail.
nodes.norm_label: assessment-trigger banner as derived valkey projection (d7)

nodes.label: LOC-Change and Recertification Orders Are Advisory (D9, D10)
nodes.rationale: M6 is the source of truth for LOC and benefit-period state with its billing and IPU implications; M11 authorizes the change and M6 executes it. Two modules touching the same table would race, and M11 enforcing the F2F window would duplicate M6's window scanner.
nodes.norm_label: loc-change and recertification orders are advisory (d9, d10)

nodes.label: EPCS Explicitly Out of Scope for M11 (D15)
nodes.rationale: EPCS is a federal regime distinct from the general CMS clinical-record signature requirement; conflating them would force every M11 signature to clear an EPCS bar that does not apply to labs, DME or supplies. M12 wraps M11's primitive with the DEA identity proofing.
nodes.norm_label: epcs explicitly out of scope for m11 (d15)

nodes.label: Per-Tenant withOrgContext Sweep Replacing Cross-Tenant Platform Scan (M11-F03)
nodes.rationale: The lab-results-overdue sweep no longer runs a cross-tenant PHI scan under withPlatformContext with no org predicate; it enumerates active org ids (non-PHI) and processes each tenant under its own withOrgContext so RLS scopes every read and write.
nodes.norm_label: per-tenant withorgcontext sweep replacing cross-tenant platform scan (m11-f03)

nodes.label: Module 12 — DoseSpot Integration & Prescribing
nodes.rationale: The medication-order and e-prescribing spine; nothing else in the system imports the DoseSpot client, talks to Surescripts, or knows about the §1311 EPCS regime. M11 + M12 together are the system the hospice nurse trusts at 2 AM.

nodes.label: medication_order Spine with med_class Discriminator (D1)
nodes.rationale: Separate-but-sibling to M11's order_record: modelling medication as just another order kind makes the data blob grow by accretion across three different regulatory regimes (CMS CoP, DEA EPCS, Surescripts SCRIPT), makes the audit denylist unmanageable and leaks EPCS into every signature path.

nodes.label: DoseSpot Adapter Boundary (full integration, not iframe)
nodes.rationale: An embedded iframe loses chart context (diagnoses, care plan, comfort-kit state), drifts prescriber identity into a separate login/timeout/audit log, hands every UI complaint to the vendor, and is a privacy-boundary nightmare for surveyors asking exactly what data left the perimeter. WardenX ships a native prescribing UI with the adapter as a thin circuit-broken pass-through that never logs bodies in the clear.
nodes.norm_label: dosespot adapter boundary (full integration, not iframe)

nodes.label: EPCS Architecture Ships, Certification Gated (D18 / ADR-006, ADR-0019 D1)
nodes.rationale: Building the architecture without the certification engagement ships the data model, audit trail and records-of-application surface today; flipping not_certified → audit_in_progress → certified is a per-tenant config change, not a redesign. A lawful Phase-1 non-EPCS path (manually-signed DEA-compliant paper Rx, or the prescriber's own external EPCS) exists so Schedule II–V comfort-kit opioids can be ordered at go-live — EPCS is an additive transmission channel, not a precondition for care.
nodes.norm_label: epcs architecture ships, certification gated (d18 / adr-006, adr-0019 d1)

nodes.label: NewRx Idempotency Key (prescriber ‖ patient ‖ rxBusinessKey, D8)
nodes.rationale: DoseSpot's NewRx is non-idempotent, so a worker retry without a key would create duplicate prescriptions at the pharmacy. The key captures 'same prescriber, same patient, same drug+strength+sig' with the sig canonicalized first so whitespace and case changes do not break dedup; keying on order ID alone would make the correction-of-record flow self-dedup and break.
nodes.norm_label: newrx idempotency key (prescriber ‖ patient ‖ rxbusinesskey, d8)

nodes.label: Refill Inbox — approval mints a NEW medication_order (D9)
nodes.rationale: Refills are new prescriptions requiring signature, so minting a new order row keeps the audit trail clean and reuses the whole sign workflow; a status flip on the source order would make a CMS surveyor read the new dispensation as a continuation.
nodes.norm_label: refill inbox — approval mints a new medication_order (d9)

nodes.label: Webhook Security Envelope (HMAC + timestamp + dedup + encryption at rest, D7)
nodes.rationale: Defense in depth: signature verifies authenticity, timestamp tolerance prevents replay with a stolen request, the (dosespot_event_id, organization_id) unique constraint ensures idempotency, and per-tenant DEK encryption protects pharmacy/prescription PHI in the body even if RLS were bypassed.
nodes.norm_label: webhook security envelope (hmac + timestamp + dedup + encryption at rest, d7)

nodes.label: MedicationHistory Persisted but Never Auto-Linked to an Order (D10)
nodes.rationale: Surescripts MedHx is an inventory of fills, not authoritative orders; auto-linking would force a clinical decision the system is not authorized to make. The reconciliation worksheet preserves clinician judgement — the same 'AI proposes, clinician approves' shape as DocLens.
nodes.norm_label: medicationhistory persisted but never auto-linked to an order (d10)

nodes.label: AI-Prohibited Zone for Medication Orders (D12)
nodes.rationale: AI Governance §2.1.1 mandates a hard block: medication errors directly harm patients and 'AI suggests, clinician decides' cannot be retrofitted onto medication mutation without a safety review that has not happened. Every approval gate has a bypass path, so the boot-time validateMedicationAIBlock() check against M32's prompt registry makes the violation impossible to ship.

nodes.label: DoseSpot Degraded Mode — Sign Always Permitted, Transmission Queues (D11)
nodes.rationale: Hospice clinicians prescribe at 2 AM and a vendor outage cannot block patient care. The clinical record — signature, audit trail, eMAR consumability — is all on our side; only pharmacy transmission can defer, so drafts persist with dosespot_send_state='queued' and drain on circuit close.
nodes.norm_label: dosespot degraded mode — sign always permitted, transmission queues (d11)

nodes.label: Module 13 — eMAR & Medication Administration
nodes.rationale: Hospice nurses give doses at 3 AM in a patient's bedroom while the family watches; the captured record is the only evidence that survives, so the bet is that bedside capture quality translates directly to patient safety and survey defensibility.

nodes.label: administration_record Spine with mode Discriminator (D1, D11)
nodes.rationale: The eMAR is always projected across M12 + M13, never stored — a materialized view goes stale the moment M12 mutates (order correction, discharge cascade). IV-continuous is a sequence of rows sharing iv_session_id rather than one mutable-rate row, because a mutable rate would violate append-only audit and mismatch the FHIR mapping.
nodes.norm_label: administration_record spine with mode discriminator (d1, d11)

nodes.label: Scheduled-Dose Materialization from sigStructured (D2)
nodes.rationale: Pre-computing puts the schedule on a query-friendly index the missed-dose sweep needs; computing on read is non-trivial across DST transitions and named-time frequencies. Past scheduled-dose rows are immutable — their existence as a 'should have happened at 0800' record is the survey-defensible trail against which administrations and misses reconcile.

nodes.label: 15-Minute Missed-Dose Detection Sweep (D4)
nodes.rationale: A per-row delayed job would put 100k+ jobs in flight at a 30-patient census; a bounded idempotent polling sweep recovers gracefully from worker outage. Detecting within 15 minutes gets the case manager an alert while there is still time to act, versus competitors' daily batch report read at QAPI a week later.

nodes.label: Controlled-Substance Witness via Separate-Device HMAC Token (D7, M13-F04)
nodes.rationale: UI-checkbox witness implementations are known to be bypassed by the clinician clicking both attestations; a separate device, session and identity is the only audit-defensible pattern. Per ADR-0019 the mandate is scoped to waste/disposal and inpatient administration — routine in-home administration by a lone clinician records the clinician's attestation plus controlled-substance accounting rather than a fabricated second witness.
nodes.norm_label: controlled-substance witness via separate-device hmac token (d7, m13-f04)

nodes.label: Comfort-Kit Deployment & Per-Medication Drawdown (D5)
nodes.rationale: The clinical record of what was used from a patient's kit is M13's domain (it is the administration trail) while physical replenishment is M21's fulfillment workflow. Competitors never reconcile the two, so a surveyor asking how the morphine in the kit was used gets a paper log from the family.

nodes.label: Medication Reconciliation as a Workflow, Not a Screen (D17)
nodes.rationale: Vendors implement reconciliation as a static form whose decisions do not structurally back-link to the resulting orders, so 'show me why this order was carried forward from home meds' gets a free-text answer. Per-line decision rows back-linking to the M12 order the prescriber signs make survey reconstruction deterministic.
nodes.norm_label: medication reconciliation as a workflow, not a screen (d17)

nodes.label: Offline Capture Queue with administeredAt vs recordedAt (D18)
nodes.rationale: Requiring connectivity pushes rural nurses to paper and breaks the timestamp trail. The clinician's wall-clock administeredAt is preserved as truth, recordedAt is server-receive, idempotency is keyed on (orgId, deviceId, localId), and the sync path re-checks M12 state so an administration against a since-discontinued order surfaces as a workflow item rather than being silently accepted or silently dropped.
nodes.norm_label: offline capture queue with administeredat vs recordedat (d18)

nodes.label: Bidirectional Consistency: M13 Asks M12 at Every Write (D6)
nodes.rationale: The data dependency runs M13 → M12 (an administration is meaningless without its order), so inverting into an M12→M13 cascade would force M12 to know M13's schema and active-administration set. A synchronous getAdministrationContext consult inside the route handler is simpler, atomic and correct; a soft advisory check is inadequate for clinical safety.
nodes.norm_label: bidirectional consistency: m13 asks m12 at every write (d6)

nodes.label: Server-Side Five-Rights Validation
nodes.rationale: Patient, drug (RxNorm crosswalk), dose, route and time are each validated against the order and the scheduled dose at write; mismatches return 422 FIVE_RIGHTS_VIOLATION naming the specific right that failed.

nodes.label: PRN Effectiveness Reassessment Trigger (M13 triggers, M9 scores — D3)
nodes.rationale: Splitting responsibility avoids M13 carrying scale-licensing logic and M9 carrying administration-lifecycle logic; M9 could not originate the trigger without subscribing to M13 anyway. Vendors' free-text 'effectiveness' box is rarely completed, never trended and never tied to a scale that measures effectiveness.
nodes.norm_label: prn effectiveness reassessment trigger (m13 triggers, m9 scores — d3)

nodes.label: Caregiver-Attested Administration with requires_rn_review (D10)
nodes.rationale: Caregivers give doses and documenting the fact is clinically and legally meaningful, but it is not the same accountability chain as clinician administration; routing it to the same cosign queue as M8 LPN/CHHA notes keeps the RN's 'things requiring my review' unified across modules.

nodes.label: AI-Prohibited Zone for Medication Administration (D15)
nodes.rationale: Extends M12's prescribing-side block to the administration side: an LLM cannot create a fake administration to mask diversion, cannot witness a controlled-substance dose, and cannot adjust a five-rights violation. HearthNote Layer 2 may narrate around an administration in read-only context only.

nodes.label: Module 14 — Interdisciplinary Group (IDG)
nodes.rationale: The operational heart of hospice clinical governance; M14's lock is the enabler that flips M7/M11/M12's already-shipped fixture-tested consumers to live production wiring.

nodes.label: IDG Meeting Lifecycle with Adjournment as Commit Point
nodes.rationale: On adjournment all in-progress decisions emit to the outbox, action items lock assignees and due dates, minutes flip to final and packet rows freeze — one atomic commit point makes the survey artifact deterministic.
nodes.norm_label: idg meeting lifecycle with adjournment as commit point

nodes.label: IDG_REQUIRED_QUORUM Evaluated Per-Decision (D3)
nodes.rationale: Evaluating quorum per-decision rather than per-meeting lets a meeting proceed while a member is briefly absent (the discussion happens) while still blocking the recording of decisions during that gap. A meeting-level check at start time falsely allows decisions recorded after a member leaves, and a coordinator-waivable quorum opens the survey-citation barn door.

nodes.label: idg_patient_packet — derived, frozen on adjournment (D1, D5, D7)
nodes.rationale: Clinicians get a fresh editable artifact pre-meeting and surveyors get a deterministic frozen snapshot after; per-patient idempotency on (meeting_id, patient_id) keeps retries safe under outbox redelivery. Discipline views are derived at build time into one row so the packet stays a single artifact to render and freeze — computing views on read would defeat both the survey artifact and the offline-mobile path.
nodes.norm_label: idg_patient_packet — derived, frozen on adjournment (d1, d5, d7)

nodes.label: Canonical idg.decision_recorded Outbox Event (D4, 9-kind discriminated union)
nodes.rationale: A single payload prevents shape drift across the four downstream consumers already locked against it, and the exhaustive union compels coordinated multi-module change for new kinds — exactly the friction wanted at the spec boundary. Per-kind topics would fragment consumers and defeat M11's one-consumer pattern; free-form jsonb would defeat compile-time exhaustiveness at consumer call sites.
nodes.norm_label: canonical idg.decision_recorded outbox event (d4, 9-kind discriminated union)

nodes.label: Action-Item Carry-Forward + Auto-Close Engine (D8)
nodes.rationale: Auto-close on a downstream artifact reaching an absorbing state prevents the 'MSW closed the loop but forgot to mark the item done' failure mode; three consecutive carry-forwards raise a critical Compliance alert because repeatedly-deferred follow-up is an OIG survey marker. The threshold is deliberately not tenant-configurable so it cannot be loosened to mask the issue.

nodes.label: idg_minutes Immutable on final + Amendment Row (D10)
nodes.rationale: Schema-level enforcement of the CoP 418.104 accurate-clinical-record invariant for the artifact surveyors most often inspect; full immutability with no amendment path is clinically untenable because misattributions and typos happen, so the M5 §164.526 amendment row makes corrections discoverable without enabling silent edits.
nodes.norm_label: idg_minutes immutable on final + amendment row (d10)

nodes.label: Per-Patient (Per-POC) 15-Day Review Floor (D17 / M14-F01)
nodes.rationale: The location-wide cadence is escapable by cancel/reschedule and is per-location, not per-POC; surveyors cite the missed review of a patient's plan of care, so the authoritative control is last_idg_reviewed_at + 15 days per included patient. CANCEL and RESCHEDULE are guarded and refused unless a covering meeting exists or an audited step-up override is recorded, and a missed review escalates rather than silently lapsing.

nodes.label: Notification Composition Moved to M36 (ADR-0024 supersedes D14–D16)
nodes.rationale: M14's v0.3 secondary role as the cross-module notification-composition layer (with its own notification_template tables) was superseded: recipient resolution and dispatch belong to M36. M14 now only emits typed alert payloads validated against M36's alert_payload_catalog and never writes to channels directly.
nodes.norm_label: notification composition moved to m36 (adr-0024 supersedes d14–d16)

nodes.label: 5-Minute Step-Up Auth on Adjournment (D13)
nodes.rationale: Adjournment is a multi-row mutating commit (decisions emit, minutes finalize, packets freeze), so the actor's identity must be fresh-verified at that moment; an unattended session at meeting end is the realistic threat. Step-up on every decision would over-burden the meeting flow where quorum plus permission already suffice.

nodes.label: Module 15 — Discipline Care Plans
nodes.rationale: The four CoP-driven discipline plans below the IDG layer — Aide POC (418.76), MSW Plan and Spiritual Care Plan (418.64), Volunteer Plan (418.78) — answering the questions M7's IPOC alone cannot: what is this aide doing, who supervises her, and can the hospice prove its volunteer ratio.

nodes.label: Aide Supervisory Visit Attestation (14-day cadence, D3, D4)
nodes.rationale: CoP 418.76(h)(1) is a hard floor tenants may tighten but never loosen. Competitors capture the supervisory visit as a free-form note on a routine RN visit, so surveyors reconstruct it by reading every narrative looking for the phrase 'supervisory visit'; M15 makes it a discrete attestation row linked to an M8 encounter with its own cadence clock, alerts at day 12/14 and an encounter-sign gate at day 16.
nodes.norm_label: aide supervisory visit attestation (14-day cadence, d3, d4)

nodes.label: Volunteer Compliance Gates as Scheduling Preconditions (D7)
nodes.rationale: The gates are the operational surface CoP 418.78 demands; M15 owns them because it owns the volunteer plan, avoiding a cross-module FK, while M17 only reads at pre-schedule time so the dependency stays single-direction. An expired TB screening flips the volunteer inactive automatically and the scheduler refuses the assignment with VOLUNTEER_GATE_UNMET.
nodes.norm_label: volunteer compliance gates as scheduling preconditions (d7)

nodes.label: 5% Volunteer Ratio is Hours ÷ Hours, Not Dollars (M15-F04 / D8)
nodes.rationale: §418.78(e) requires volunteer services to equal ≥5% of total patient-care HOURS of paid and contract staff, so numerator and denominator are both hours — minutes ÷ dollars is dimensionally meaningless. Dollars are confined to the separate cost-savings evidence artifact (ARCH-064). The numerator is direct-care volunteer_visit durations plus a typed volunteer_admin_hours source replacing the unexplained manual_adjustment.
nodes.norm_label: 5% volunteer ratio is hours ÷ hours, not dollars (m15-f04 / d8)

nodes.label: Parent-IPOC Reference with Discipline-Only Refinement (D5)
nodes.rationale: A nullable parent_goal_id supports discipline-only additions (a chaplain's family-spiritual-support goal with no IPOC parent) while preserving traceability back to the IPOC; requiring the parent would force the IPOC to anticipate every discipline-only goal, and copying IPOC content into the discipline plan would be a denormalization disaster on IPOC updates.

nodes.label: Per-Plan-Kind RequiredSignerSet, CHHA Acknowledges Not Cosigns (D11)
nodes.rationale: CoP 418.76 has the supervising RN author the POC and the aide acknowledge they will execute it; a cosign would imply equal authorship the regulation does not grant. Chaplain self-sign matches autonomous spiritual-care responsibility, while MSW and Volunteer plans carry an RN cosign for IDG alignment because the RN is the case manager.
nodes.norm_label: per-plan-kind requiredsignerset, chha acknowledges not cosigns (d11)

nodes.label: family_violence_disclosure_allowed ABAC Predicate (D9)
nodes.rationale: SUD content reuses M7's sud_disclosure_allowed to keep the consent surface unified, but family-violence content has separate state-law gating (mandatory-reporter posture plus non-disclosure to family-member portal users) so it needs its own predicate. Both filter at the SQL WHERE level, never post-fetch, avoiding 'data loaded but UI-hidden' leaks.

nodes.label: No M15 Table Is Partitioned (D13 / M15-F06, ADR-0022 D1.1)
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL requires a partitioned table's unique constraints to include the partition key, which the partial uniques on discipline_care_plan and discipline_assessment would violate. The original 'high-volume, grows unbounded' rationale was factually wrong: a current-state root caps at ≤4 rows per admission, so partitioning was pure cost and would force cross-partition reads on every 'find the current row'.
nodes.norm_label: no m15 table is partitioned (d13 / m15-f06, adr-0022 d1.1)

nodes.label: Five Outbound Seams (DisciplinePlanReader, MswRiskFactorReader, VolunteerComplianceProvider, SupervisoryCadenceReader, DisciplineComplianceProvider)
nodes.rationale: The M7/M9/M10/M11 precedent: the owning module publishes its seams and consumers (M14/M16/M17/M22/M27/M28) wire when they land. M15 cannot be gated on six downstream modules because CoP 418.76 supervisory enforcement is go-live blocking.
nodes.norm_label: five outbound seams (disciplineplanreader, mswriskfactorreader, volunteercomplianceprovider, supervisorycadencereader, disciplinecomplianceprovider)

nodes.label: M8 Owns Visit Narrative; M15 Owns the Supervisory Attestation (D4)
nodes.rationale: The architecture's DisciplineVisit listing was schematic — the visit encounter lives in M8 per its own type enum. Splitting narrative between M8 and M15 would break the ownership boundary and force M14's aggregator to merge content from two modules; the supervisory attestation is a discrete artifact in CMS surveyor language, so it earns its own row.
nodes.norm_label: m8 owns visit narrative; m15 owns the supervisory attestation (d4)

nodes.label: Fail-CLOSED Volunteer/Supervisory Gate Semantics During Outage (M15-F11)
nodes.rationale: During a DR degradation the gate denies with an audited override path rather than fail-open booking of non-compliant volunteers.
nodes.norm_label: fail-closed volunteer/supervisory gate semantics during outage (m15-f11)

nodes.label: Encounter Lifecycle State Machine & Layer-3 Signing Gate
nodes.rationale: draft → finalized → signed → cosign_pending → cosigned with addendum_open and voided branches. Before any encounter signs, the always-on Layer 3 gate checks required HearthNote sections per encounter type × discipline, required vitals, required HOPE items, required scales, the LPN/CHHA cosignature row, the late-entry reason, and fresh step-up authentication; failures return 422 with structured remediation hints.
nodes.norm_label: encounter lifecycle state machine & layer-3 signing gate

nodes.label: Read-Time Trend Computation, Materialization Deferred (D4)
nodes.rationale: One patient × one scale × 90 days is rarely more than ~30 rows, so a materialized view would add replication lag, an invalidation surface and a second source of truth for IDG and HOPE reads; read-time computation also lets corrections take effect immediately.

nodes.label: Nullable source_encounter_id Forward Seam (D5)
nodes.rationale: M9 has standalone clinical value (telephonic check-ins, IDG-only review, retrospective paper entry), and blocking M9 on M8 would block M7 → IDG which already consumes LatestAssessmentProvider. Synthesizing a virtual encounter would add a ghost row M8 later has to reconcile.

nodes.label: Outbox-Only Cross-Module Communication Rule (D6, D8)
nodes.rationale: Outbox publication is the only cross-module communication M11 performs; it never calls another module's HTTP route. Direct HTTP between domain modules introduces fan-out, latency variance and partial-failure modes, whereas outbox plus idempotency dedup gives at-least-once delivery with deterministic side effects. Polling another module's tables would be a schema-import violation and a retrograde dependency.

nodes.label: Per-Tenant DoseSpot Clinic Credentials (D5)
nodes.rationale: One shared DoseSpot clinic would conflate tenants and break Surescripts's per-prescriber identity model; credentials load from the secrets manager at boot with no plaintext on disk in production, and boot validation that every enrolled tenant has credentials fails fast.

nodes.label: Outbox-Driven DoseSpot Patient Sync (D4)
nodes.rationale: M5 is the system of record for demographics and emits events without knowing M12 exists; M12 subscribes without M5 knowing. M5 calling DoseSpot directly would violate the M5 boundary (M5 has no DoseSpot import), and a polled diff worker would be heavier with more latency. The upsert is idempotent, keyed on wardenx_patient_id.
